summary: The College Financial Aid Clarity Act of 2025 requires the Department of Education to create a standardized, consumer-tested format for financial aid offers. Starting on July 1, 2029, colleges and universities that receive federal financial assistance must use this standardized format and consistent terminology for all paper and electronic financial aid offers and related communications.

affected_groups.effect: Receive standardized, clearer financial aid offers detailing costs, grants, net prices, and loans across all participating institutions.
Must modify financial aid offer forms, communications, and portals to comply with federal formatting, terminology, and disclosure rules by July 1, 2029.
Must conduct consumer testing, publish requirements by July 1, 2028, notify schools, and periodically review a sample of financial aid offers for compliance.

key_provisions: Requires the Department of Education to establish a consumer testing process with various stakeholders to design a simple and understandable financial aid offer format.
Mandates that all financial aid offers include specific cost information, grant and scholarship amounts, net price calculations, loan details, and student employment opportunities.
Requires colleges to provide supplemental content and disclosures regarding renewability conditions, changes from outside aid, and loan repayment terms.
Directs institutions to use the title 'Financial Aid Offer', plain language, and specific formatting rules that clearly separate required costs from other expenses and distinguish grants from loans.
Prohibits institutions from treating an electronic receipt confirmation as an official acceptance or rejection of the financial aid offer.
Requires the Department of Education to collect and review a random representative sample of institutional financial aid offers every other year starting July 1, 2029.
missing_information: Specific funding amounts or administrative costs required to carry out the consumer testing and compliance reviews.
Penalties for institutions of higher education that fail to comply with the financial aid offer formatting and disclosure requirements.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The College Financial Aid Clarity Act of 2025 requires the Department of Education to create a standardized, consumer-tested format for financial aid offers. Starting on July 1, 2029, colleges and universities that receive federal financial assistance must use this standardized format and consistent terminology for all paper and electronic financial aid offers and related communications.
summary_detail.significance: This bill standardizes how colleges present financial costs and aid packages to students, aiming to make student financial aid offers uniform, transparent, and easier to compare across different institutions.

title: College Financial Aid Clarity Act of 2025
